detailed_rationale:
CE Info Systems (MapmyIndia) is India's leading indigenous digital-mapping and geospatial-data company, with a real competitive moat: proprietary map data, government/PSU preference under India's data-localization and Atmanirbhar policy push, and embedded-navigation deals with auto OEMs plus IoT/fleet-tracking contracts. Historically this supported strong growth (25% 5-year, 19% 3-year revenue CAGR), which is exactly why our growth-divergence flag is triggered now: FY26 revenue grew just 2% (Rs.474 Cr vs Rs.463 Cr) and net profit actually fell 9% (Rs.134 Cr vs Rs.148 Cr) -- a sharp, real deceleration from the historical trend, not a rounding effect, likely reflecting the lumpiness of large enterprise/government contract timing rather than a structural moat failure, but we have no direct evidence in hand of a reacceleration catalyst.

An earnings-quality flag: Other Income of Rs.52 Cr in FY26 is large enough, relative to Rs.134 Cr net profit, that a meaningful share of reported profit is treasury/interest income on the company's cash balance rather than core mapping/IoT operations -- worth noting explicitly since it means underlying operating profitability is weaker than the headline PAT suggests. Working capital has also deteriorated (61 to 93 days), consistent with slower enterprise/government collections. The balance sheet itself is clean (near debt-free, Rs.7 Cr borrowings), and promoter holding is stable (~51.4%).

Reverse-DCF: at ~48-64x earnings (our CSV shows 48x, Screener's more current pull shows ~64x), the market is still pricing MapmyIndia as a growth compounder, but FY26's actual print was flat-to-declining EPS. Unless the enterprise/government order pipeline reaccelerates meaningfully, this multiple is not supported by the demonstrated trend, and we would need to see at least two quarters of reacceleration before crediting a return to the historical growth rate.
recommendation_rationale: The quant Sell is corroborated: the growth-divergence flag (69.3 on the 3-year growth score vs just 15.7 on the 1-year) matches a real, verified deceleration in the actual FY26 results (+2% revenue, -9% profit), a meaningful share of profit is now treasury income rather than core operations, and the ~48-64x multiple still prices in a growth rate the business has not delivered in its most recent full year. We do not see grounds to rescue this to Hold absent evidence of reacceleration.
summary: CE Info Systems (MapmyIndia) is India's leading indigenous digital-mapping company with a real data and policy moat, but FY26 growth stalled sharply -- revenue grew just 2% and profit actually declined 9%, a marked slowdown from its historical 19-25% growth rates, and a meaningful share of even that reduced profit came from interest income on cash rather than core operations. At roughly 48-64 times earnings, the stock is still priced for a growth rate it did not deliver this past year. We rate this a Sell pending evidence of reacceleration.
positive_para: A genuine, defensible moat in proprietary Indian map data and geospatial IP, government/PSU tailwinds from data-localization policy, embedded-navigation relationships with domestic auto OEMs, and a clean, debt-free balance sheet with stable promoter ownership (~51.4%).
negative_para: FY26 revenue grew only 2% and net profit fell 9%, a sharp break from the historical 19-25% growth trend that the stock's ~48-64x multiple still assumes; a large share of even the reduced profit (Rs.52 Cr of Rs.134 Cr) came from interest/treasury income rather than core mapping or IoT operations, and working capital days worsened from 61 to 93, consistent with slower enterprise and government collections. Contract lumpiness may explain the slowdown, but we have no confirmed evidence yet of a reacceleration.
reverse_dcf_judgment: A 48-64x multiple prices continued double-digit growth; FY26 delivered +2% revenue and -9% profit. Unless enterprise/government order timing reaccelerates meaningfully in the next few quarters, the current price is rich relative to the demonstrated (as opposed to historical) growth rate.
